tool.name: Define haplotype windows
tool.description: size read-level haplotype windows from the fragment-length distribution of a cohort
tool.command: @REF_RESOLVE@ ## Windows must be identical across every specimen or the resulting sheets have ## non-corresponding columns, so this is a COHORT-level reduction over the BAM ## collection, deliberately not a per-specimen step. mkdir -p bams && #for $i, $b in enumerate($bams) ln -s '$b' 'bams/${i}.bam' && ln -s '${b.metadata.bam_index}' 'bams/${i}.bam.bai' && #end for pyeuk define-windows --ref '$ref_path' --bams bams/*.bam --sample $sample --min-spanning $min_spanning #if str($legacy_spanning_target).strip() != '' --spanning-target $legacy_spanning_target #end if --min-depth $min_depth --window-min $window_min --window-max $window_max --width-step $width_step #if int($step) > 0 --step $step #end if --out '$windows'

param.name: bams
param.label: Aligned BAMs (the cohort)
param.help: A collection or several datasets. A sample of these is scanned; all of them get the same windows.

expand.label: Reference the BAMs were aligned to
expand.help: The reference the BAMs were mapped to: a FASTA from your history, or a genome cached on this Galaxy.

param.label: How many BAMs to scan
param.help: How many BAMs to scan. 0 = all.

param.label: Minimum fraction of reads that span a window
param.help: Widest width at which at least this fraction of overlapping reads span the window end to end.

param.name: legacy_spanning_target
param.label: Legacy percentile rule (leave empty)
param.help: Deprecated. Set a value only to reproduce a pre-2026-08 run; it overrides the measured rule above.

param.label: Depth for a position to count as covered
param.help: Minimum read depth for a base to count toward a window.

param.label: Maximum window length (0 = no cap)
param.help: Longest window to try (bases). Longer windows carry more linkage but accumulate sequencing error; worth checking per panel. 0 = unbounded.

param.label: Tiling step (0 = non-overlapping)
param.help: Spacing between windows. 0 = one window per reference sequence.

tool.help:
Identifies data-adaptive sub-amplicon analysis windows directly from the read alignments, with no pre-annotated locus boundaries. Windows are chosen once for the whole cohort so every specimen is evaluated over the same intervals.
In amplicon sequencing the forward and reverse reads start at different primer positions and overlap asymmetrically. Pinning a window to the first covered base restricts spanning coverage to one strand; maximising width alone selects intervals that starve one orientation. This tool optimises placement and width together to keep the window as long as possible while both strands still span it.
Per reference sequence it evaluates three properties: coverage extent, placement, and width. The extent runs from the first to the last position with read depth at least min_depth across the sampled specimens. Candidate intervals are scored by ``S = width x f_span``, where f_span is the fraction of overlapping reads that span the interval end to end (kept above min_spanning). f_span is measured from the CIGAR alignments, not inferred from nominal read length. The extent is then tiled at the chosen width; leading or trailing remnants that meet the minimum width are kept as adjacent windows.
Input: aligned BAMs for the cohort, and the reference they were mapped to. Output: a BED of windows, used by Call window haplotypes. @HELP_FOOTER@
